summary: Hosted service, sprint 1x: the candidate's review edits reach the approved and exported CV. Approving builds the next version with the latest edit of each block, runs the final CV checks again on it, and binds and exports that version; the desktop, the CLI and the API all pass the edits recorded against the reviewed version. Edited blocks keep an edited mark before and after approval, and the approval footer says which version approving makes. A CV header that still shows placeholders such as [Your name] blocks approval again, so the candidate replaces them with an edit or overrides with a reason. When the only failing final check is the word-match miss behind gaps already marked as known, Approve records those reasons without a separate override. An open web tab offers a reload when a new release is serving. The release also carries reasoning levels per role (milestone 57): GPT-6.1 Terra replaces GPT-6.1 Sol as the Balanced reviewer, the model editor offers Writer and Reviewer reasoning levels, the start confirmation and run details name each role's level, and credit rule v2 doubles a run's base when either role runs at high, extra high or max. Patch 0.9.1 fixes the web model dialog, which refused to apply any preset that changed the workspace pair (such as Balanced with its new reviewer) because it took the hosted service's server-held consent for a stale screen acknowledgement; a refusal from the host now names its reason. The cost scenario names each role's model instead of an internal profile id, and the known-gaps action no longer overflows its box.
knownLimitations: Staging only: production keeps its earlier images until the owner deploys this tag there. Staging runs behind the owner token, so sign-in, plans and credits, and record export and deletion are not exercised there until the identity provider is hosted; credit rule v2 is proven by tests only. The critic does not review the candidate's edits, and accepting a finding after the last round still changes nothing in the export. No paid run has measured what a raised reasoning level costs or adds, GPT-6.1 Terra as the reviewer is unvalidated, and workspaces saved on the old Balanced pair show a custom pair until Balanced is applied again. The cost of a complete cached run is still to measure (#1597).
